newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan initially oks Big Three banks' 97/98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan initially oks Big Three banks' 97/98 budget.

text.p: Taiwan authorities said on Tuesday they had given an initial nod for the Big Three state banks' 1997/98 budgets, which plan for a doubling of pre-tax profits on gains from selling off shares of state firms.
The budgets for the three state giants are being reviewed by a panel under the Taiwan provincial government, officials said.

The body agreed that in view of the planned share sell-off, Chang Hwa Bank's 1997/98 (July/June) pre-tax profit target should be revised upward to T$13.3 billion from an initially planned T$5.8 billion, an official of the provincial government's finance department told Reuters.
Likewise, First Bank's target will rise to T$14.8 billion from T$7.3 billion and Hua Nan Bank's to T$14.4 billion from T$7 billion, the official said.

The sharp profit target increases reflected plans by four firms owned by the provincial government to begin privatising in June. The process of privatisation through listing on the main Taiwan Stock Exchange was expected to take two years.
"By selling their share holdings in the four state firms, the Big Three banks will see their profits soar," the official said.

The provincial government now owns 93 percent of the Medium Business Bank of Taiwan and 100 percent of the other three firms: Taiwan Development and Trust Corp, Taiwan Fire and Marine Insurance Co and Taiwan Life Insurance Co.
The government plans to offer 15 percent of Medium Business Bank in its initial public offering and will offer 30 percent stakes of the other three firms in their IPOs, he said.
"In the second stage, about two years after listing, the government plans to lower state stakes in the four firms to 30 percent each, thus privatising them," the official said.
He said detailed share release plans were not yet available.
The new targets for the Big Three banks' pre-tax profits are more than double their 1996/97 profit targets.
For 1996/97, the pre-tax profit target at Chang Hwa is T$6.15 billion, T$7.31 billion at First Bank and T$7.1 billion at Hua Nan, officials in the three banks said.
The budget plans need final approval by the provincial government and provincial assembly, the official said.
